theory.intro: The **Medicare levy** is an extra tax that helps fund Australia's public health scheme. It is a flat $2\%$ of taxable income, whatever the income, and is added to the income tax payable.
facts: $2\%$ as a decimal is $0.02$, so the levy is $0.02\times\text{Taxable income}$.
The levy is charged on taxable income, never on gross income, so subtract the allowable deductions first.
Because the rate never changes, a rise of $\$10\,000$ in taxable income always adds exactly $\$200$ to the levy.
steps: Multiply the taxable income by the levy rate

foundation.question_text:
A physiotherapist has a taxable income of $\$74\,300$.
Calculate her Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.

A hospital pharmacist has a taxable income of $\$88\,415$.
Calculate his Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.

An aged-care service manager has a taxable income of $\$196\,750$.
Calculate her Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.

A part-time carer has a taxable income of $\$21\,450$.
Calculate her Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.

A social worker has a gross income of $\$68\,900$ and allowable tax deductions of $\$1150$.
Calculate his Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Find the taxable income**
$\text{Taxable income}=68\,900-1150$
$=\$67\,750$
2. **Multiply the taxable income by the levy rate**
$\text{Medicare levy}=0.02\times67\,750$
$=\$1355.00$

foundation.question_text:
An occupational therapist earned a salary of $\$81\,240$ and $\$385$ in bank interest. She claims union fees of $\$720$ and work equipment of $\$1105$.
Calculate her Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Find the taxable income**
$\text{Taxable income}=(81\,240+385)-(720+1105)$
$=81\,625-1825$
$=\$79\,800$
2. **Multiply the taxable income by the levy rate**
$\text{Medicare levy}=0.02\times79\,800$
$=\$1596.00$

foundation.question_text:
A speech pathologist has a taxable income of $\$71\,600$ and her income tax payable is $\$14\,832$.
Calculate her total tax payable, including the Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.

A community support worker paid a Medicare levy of $\$1247.60$.
Calculate his taxable income, to the nearest dollar.

development.question_text:
A physiotherapist is paid $\$3145$ per fortnight and has allowable tax deductions of $\$1690$ for the year.
Calculate her Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.
development.solution_text:
1. **Find the taxable income**
$\text{Gross income}=3145\times26$
$=\$81\,770$
$\text{Taxable income}=81\,770-1690$
$=\$80\,080$
2. **Multiply the taxable income by the levy rate**
$\text{Medicare levy}=0.02\times80\,080$
$=\$1601.60$

development.question_text:
A community pharmacist has a taxable income of $\$96\,455$ and her income tax payable is $\$21\,844.75$.
Calculate her total tax payable, including the Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.

An aged-care nurse paid a Medicare levy of $\$1533.40$ and claimed allowable tax deductions of $\$2180$.
Calculate her gross income, to the nearest dollar.

An occupational therapist's taxable income rises from $\$79\,500$ to $\$92\,300$.
Calculate how much more Medicare levy she now pays, to the nearest cent.
development.solution_text:
The levy rate is the same at both incomes, so only the increase is levied.
$\text{Extra levy}=0.02\times(92\,300-79\,500)$
$=0.02\times12\,800$
$=\$256.00$

mastery.question_text:
Two allied health workers have taxable incomes that differ by $\$18\,000$.
By finding the levies for taxable incomes of $\$62\,000$ and $\$80\,000$, and then for $\$134\,000$ and $\$152\,000$, show that the difference between their Medicare levies is the same in both cases, and explain why.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Levy on }\$62\,000=0.02\times62\,000$
$=\$1240.00$
$\text{Levy on }\$80\,000=0.02\times80\,000$
$=\$1600.00$
$\text{Difference}=1600-1240$
$=\$360.00$
$\text{Levy on }\$134\,000=0.02\times134\,000$
$=\$2680.00$
$\text{Levy on }\$152\,000=0.02\times152\,000$
$=\$3040.00$
$\text{Difference}=3040-2680$
$=\$360.00$
The levy rate is a flat $2\%$ at every income, so the difference depends only on the $\$18\,000$ gap: $0.02\times18\,000=\$360.00$ whatever the two incomes are.

mastery.question_text:

Use the tax table to calculate her total tax payable, including the Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.

$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
